responsibilities.name: Weekly Executive Update
responsibilities.instruction: Produce this week's Weekly Executive Update to structure the 30-minute weekly executive sync. Read your source folder, the four designated meetings, the output folder and the brand-guide doc id from core memory (do not look up a 'process' document; do not use the calendar). For each designated meeting read ONLY the most recent Transcript doc (skip the Recording video) and SAVE its full text to a working file; then synthesize a COMPLETE briefing — agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due table — where every section carries real content drawn from the transcripts (no empty or placeholder sections). Deliver it as ONE branded Google Doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <date>' in the output folder (ids copied verbatim) and report the shareable link plus the section headings you read back.
responsibilities.success_criteria: This week's Weekly Executive Update exists as a branded Google Doc TITLED 'Weekly Executive Update - <date>' (not the legacy 'Weekly Executive Brief') in the exec-summaries output folder, and its shareable link is reported. As evidence, the agent READ THE FINISHED DOCUMENT BACK and reported the exact section headings AND confirmed each has real, non-empty body content synthesized from the transcripts — an empty-section or placeholder document does NOT satisfy this. Required sections: agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due Action Items table. Sourced ONLY from the four designated weekly meetings (no other meeting), acronyms normalized (e.g. SOC 2), and if this week's doc already existed it was updated, not duplicated. The read-back (headings + non-empty bodies + link) is the proof.

context.purpose: Leadership runs a 30-minute weekly executive sync and needs one reliable, skimmable briefing, built the same way every week from that week's meeting notes.
process: READ MEMORY (do this first, with core-memory-read): load this deployment's weekly-exec specifics from your core memory (category resources) — the shared meeting-notes SOURCE folder id, the FOUR designated source meetings with each meeting's subfolder id, the exec-summaries OUTPUT folder id, and the brand-guide doc id. These live in memory; 'the process' is THIS list of steps, not a document to look up. If a required id is missing from memory, say so and stop rather than guessing or using the calendar.

GATHER — transcripts only, saved to the workspace: for EACH of the four designated meetings, open its subfolder and pick the single MOST RECENT occurrence by date. Read ONLY the Google Doc whose name ends '- Transcript' (the notes) — SKIP the '- Recording' video/mp4, which cannot be read as text. Save each transcript's FULL text to a file in your working directory (docs-cat <id> --out <meeting>.txt). Capturing the full text to disk is REQUIRED: the document body must be written from the full transcripts, and a summary passed between steps loses the substance. Use ONLY these four meetings; EXCLUDE every other meeting in the space, even if more recent. (This week the Operations Sync source is a single doc id held in memory.) If one of the four has no occurrence this week, note that briefly.

SYNTHESIZE from the SAVED transcript files (never from a summary): read the saved files back and distill them into a content JSON in the docs-create-branded --content format — an array of section objects such as {"type":"heading","level":2,"text":"..."}, {"type":"paragraph","text":"..."}, {"type":"bullet_list","items":["..."]}, {"type":"table","headers":[...],"rows":[[...]]}. EVERY heading MUST be followed by paragraph/bullet/table sections carrying the ACTUAL substance from the transcripts — specific decisions, owners, risks, dates, numbers. NEVER emit a heading with no body, and never use placeholder text ('Project X', 'TBD'); an empty or placeholder section is a FAILURE. Cover, in order: Agenda-at-a-Glance (segments + time boxes + leads, ~30 min); a short State of the Week (what shipped, biggest risk, focus, binding constraint); per-area status grouped Client Delivery, Platform & Engineering, Operations & Business, blockers inline; Decisions to Lock; and an owner/action/due Action Items table (5-10 top items). Normalize acronyms (e.g. 'Sock 2' -> SOC 2). About three pages.

DELIVER in one step, from the JSON you just built: create the branded doc with docs-create-branded --title "Weekly Executive Update - <this week's date, YYYY-MM-DD>" --content <your content json file> --brand-doc <brand-guide id from memory> --folder <output folder id from memory>. Title it 'Weekly Executive Update - <date>' — NOT 'Weekly Executive Brief' or any other name. Copy every id EXACTLY from memory (verbatim, character-for-character). If a Weekly Executive Update for THIS week already exists in the output folder, update it instead of creating a duplicate.

VERIFY with evidence: read the finished doc back and report (a) the section headings AND, for each, that it has real non-empty body content — an empty-section doc does NOT count as done; (b) the four source transcripts you used; (c) the shareable link. That read-back is the proof.
